# NSPanel HAUI 0.5.2

Version 0.5.2 fixes several schedule problems, adds a dashboard card and six colorful predefined themes, splits the device settings into groups behind a tile grid, and tidies the editor's forms, Fleet and the Updates sidebar. It includes the Home Assistant integration, editor and firmware; the firmware only carries the new version number, and the display TFT files are unchanged.

## Before updating

One stored setting may change by itself. A schedule entry that sets its own dimmed brightness now needs the device's **Brightness dimmed**. When the integration loads the panel store, it sets **Brightness dimmed** to 20 % (the panel's default) on every device whose schedule needs it and logs a warning. After updating, check the value under **Screen** in the device settings. See [the upgrade notes](docs/user/update.md#a-schedule-entry-that-dims-needs-a-dimmed-brightness).

No TFT update is needed; the release continues to require display version 0.4.5.

## Breaking changes

- **Dimmed brightness for a schedule** — in 0.5.0 a schedule entry could set a dimmed brightness while the device left **Brightness dimmed** empty, to keep the value set on the panel. The hub then had nothing to restore when the entry ended, and the panel kept the entry's dimmed brightness. The device setting is now required for such an entry: it is the dimmed brightness outside the entry. Stored devices are migrated as described above. A configuration that sets an entry's dimmed brightness without the device setting is refused when it is saved. When you give an entry a dimmed brightness in the **Schedule** group while the device has none, the group takes the panel's **Brightness Dimmed** reading (20 % when the panel reports none), says so, and saves it with the settings.

## Added

- **Dashboard card** — `custom:nspanel-haui-card` puts a device's home panel or its live screen on any dashboard, view-only, for every signed-in user and without admin rights. See [Dashboard Card](docs/user/dashboard-card.md).
- **Predefined themes** — six colorful themes beside the neutral **Dark**, **Light**, **White** and **Black**: **Midnight**, **Ocean**, **Forest**, **Sunset**, **Violet** and the light **Sky**. Each one sets every semantic page color — header, background, text, components and entity states — and the theme's own page background picks whether it draws the light or the dark weather, alarm and climate icon palette, so page and icons always match. See [Themes](docs/user/configuration/themes.md).
- **Device settings groups** — the device settings open on a grid of tiles, one per group, each naming in a few words what its group holds: **General** (model, language, formats, theme), **Screen** (brightness values, the timeouts and the schedule), **Sounds**, **Home & idle**, **Gestures**, **Screen buttons**, **Hardware buttons** and **Advanced**. A tile opens the group's own page, and the sidebar strip's back arrow returns to the grid; **Save** and **Cancel** stay in the footer, so the whole device is one draft. See [Device Settings](docs/user/configuration/device.md#device-settings).
- **Selecting a device on Fleet** — select a **Device inventory** row anywhere outside its name and buttons (or press Enter or Space while it has focus), or the name strip under a device card. The row and the card are highlighted together, so a device is easy to find in both, and selecting a row scrolls the cards to it. The selected card stays centered when you return from the device. Select it again to clear the selection. The card's screen still opens the device.
- **Schedule in the device settings** — the **Schedule** group sits at the end of **Screen**, below the brightness, dimming and display-off fields its entries fill their empty fields from, so the values an entry inherits are shown once, as the fields themselves. Before, the sidebar repeated them read-only under **Outside the entries**. **Schedule** and **Gestures** are groups of the device settings instead of sidebars of their own, and the device's theme choice sits in **General**; all of them are part of the settings draft, so the settings' one **Save** applies them and **Cancel** discards them. See [Schedule](docs/user/configuration/device.md#schedule) and [Gestures](docs/user/configuration/device.md#gestures).
- **Move to another device** — the panel's **More** menu holds **Move to…**, a submenu of the hub's other devices. Moving keeps the panel's key unless the target device already uses it; the confirmation names the free key it got instead. Settings of the old device that name the panel (home and idle panels, gestures and items that open it) keep the key, as after **Delete**, and popups a device extends stay with that device. The submenu is keyboard accessible: ArrowRight opens it, ArrowLeft returns to the menu. See [The Panel List](docs/user/configuration/README.md#the-panel-list).
- **Per-state values** — an item's name, icon, color and value, and a grid tile's colors, switch between **One value** and **Per state**. **Per state** shows one row per entity state, suggested by the state field, instead of typed JSON; a state without a row keeps the default, and switching back keeps the current state's value. See [Values that depend on the state](docs/user/configuration/items.md#values-that-depend-on-the-state).
- **Latest events reset** — the timeline's second line names the device it is scoped to and closes with the window it covers (**Last 24 hours**, or **Since 14:32** after a reset), and the title line carries **Reset**, which restarts the list at the moment you press it instead of the last 24 hours, with **Last 24 hours** to go back. See [Logs](docs/user/configuration/README.md#logs).
- **Device inventory footer** — the inventory closes with one connection segment per device in its connection tone, so a full fleet's state reads at a glance under the table.

## Changed

- **Entity names** — Home Assistant puts the device name in front of an entity's full name, so the editor showed names such as *NSPanel Salon Lampa Kuchnia*. The entity picker, item lists, the **Diagnostics** entity list and the preview's entity tooltip now show the entity's own name (*Lampa Kuchnia*). Typing the full name in the entity picker still finds the entity.
- **Switches** — every switch in the editor sits at the right end of its row, after its label: device settings, panel and item options, schedule entries, update settings and the **Device Enabled** switch.
- **Type** — the editor uses one type scale at Home Assistant's sizes: the title bar and page titles 20px, sidebar titles 18px, card and section titles 16px, names, values and labels 14px in one weight, hints and meta 13px. Every size follows the Home Assistant font size setting.
- **Panel count** — the panel list's group headings say **Navigation (1 panel)** instead of **Navigation (1 panels)**.
- **Device settings** — the fields are split across the groups of the tile grid behind the settings, and each field takes its own row. **Screen** lists the brightness values, the dimming timeout and duration and the display-off timeout first, then the auto dimming and auto display-off switches and the schedule; **Home & idle** shows the **Home panel** and **Idle panels** pickers at the right edge of their row, followed by **Auto page** and its timeout; **General** carries the display model, language and formats beside the theme.
- **Backups, Updates and Themes** — each opens a sidebar of its own from a button below the **Connection** and **Diagnostics** cards, so the **Connection** card (formerly **Connection & device**) keeps only the readings. Each button spans the whole width of the sidebar on a line of its own; **Updates** and **Themes** also name what they hold on their trailing edge — what the update settings hold, the selected theme's name. **Themes** replaces **Edit theme**.
- **Import and Export** — the **Backup** card is gone. Its **Import** and **Export** buttons moved into a **Backups** sidebar of their own, which the new **Backups** button below **Themes** opens: one card per direction, with **Import** naming what it replaces and that there is no undo.
- **Update settings** — the **Update channel** is a list, and **Install firmware updates automatically** is a switch that replaces **When a new version is found** (**Manual** or **Auto**). It comes after **Check for a new version**. The stored setting (`firmware_auto_update`) is unchanged.
- **Updates sidebar** — an offered firmware or display update turns the installed version into one badge with the version it updates to (`0.5.2 → 0.5.3`), in place of a separate **Update available** badge and the latest-release note. The integration's version moved from its own row to the end of the **Check for updates** row and shows while updates are off too; the integration updates through the Marketplace, so the sidebar has nothing to install for it. On a narrow sidebar (the default width, or a phone) the row reads **Check** and shows the version alone, **Install** shows only its icon and the badge shows only the new version.
- **Fleet layout** — the dashboard uses the full width of a wide window instead of stopping at 1440 px. The **Device inventory** grows with its devices; a long list scrolls under its column headings, which stay in view. **Latest events** beside it takes the inventory's height and scrolls inside it; on a narrow window, where the two cards stack, it keeps a height of its own.
- **Fleet carousel** — the device row always fades its right edge, which shows that more cards follow. Where the devices end before the row does, dashed card outlines fill the remaining width instead of empty space.
- **Latest events and Logs** — **Latest events** lists only the last 24 hours' warnings and errors; the full log, info and debug included, is the **Logs** sidebar. A device selected on the dashboard scopes both to it; without a selection both list every device, and the timeline names that scope **All devices**.
- **Device screen** — the **Connection** and **Diagnostics** tiles show their values in smaller text, and the Wi-Fi signal bars stand at the tile's edge beside the label and value instead of after the value. The Wi-Fi icon shows the strength the panel last reported even while the hub is disconnected, and the status dot keeps the connection state; the uptime tile is green while the panel is online and stable.
- **Integration, not hub** — the Updates sidebar and the panel's About page already call the Home Assistant side the *integration*; Fleet and **Diagnostics** now do too. The summary strip on Fleet shows **Integration version** instead of **Hub version**, and **Diagnostics** shows the **Integration log** tile and **Integration details** instead of **Hub log** and **Hub details**. A report made with **Copy report** heads its log lines *Recent integration log*.
- **Panel overview** — with no panel selected, the Panels view's side card shows a tile for the **Home panel** and one for the **Idle panel**. Each tile now shows the role's icon on its left with the role and the panel stacked beside it; before, the panel sat under a row of icon and role. On a narrow card the two tiles stack, so a long panel name keeps its room.

## Fixed

### Schedule

- **Dimmed brightness after an entry** — an entry's dimmed brightness no longer stays after the entry ends; see *Breaking changes*.
- **Auto display off** — saving the device settings with a changed **Auto display off** while an entry was active wrote the panel's switch a second time and could override the entry. While the schedule has entries, it now owns the switch alone. When you remove every entry, the integration sets the switch once from **Auto display off**; after that, automations control it again.
- **Daylight saving time** — on the day the clocks change, the time to the next entry was counted on the wall clock, so an entry could start an hour early or late. It now starts on time.
- **Polar night** — where the sun did not rise or set until the next day, the hub stopped looking for the next sunrise or sunset entry and resumed only after the panel reconnected. It now looks again every day.

### Editor

- **Home Assistant app** — in the Home Assistant app the strip under the phone's status bar showed the page background above the editor's title bar. The editor now handles the screen insets itself: the strip takes the header colour, and the content keeps clear of the screen's side edges and the home indicator.
- **Entity hover on Row panels** — with **Show entities in the preview** on, only a row's icon and name named its entity. The row's buttons, switch and slider now name it too.
- **Entity hover on hardware buttons** — hovering a hardware button in the preview now names the entity it switches: its entity when one is set without relay mode, otherwise its relay.
- **Entity hover in Live mode** — the entity hover worked only in the Simulated preview; in the Live preview it raised an error on every mouse move. The Live preview now names the entity under the mouse as well.
- **Missing entities** — a widget whose entity Home Assistant does not have was not named at all. It is named now, and the tooltip says when an entity is not found or unavailable, which explains why the panel shows it as unavailable.
- **Accessibility** — the dashboard meets WCAG AA contrast for status text, badges, icons and the primary button in light and dark themes. A screen reader hears event levels, the page heading, named device cards and table columns, and rollout changes.

### Updates

- **Translations** — the reasons a firmware update is withheld or refused (the panel and the release are different build variants, the panel reports no or an invalid firmware version, the manifest names no build variant) and the panel's notice that a firmware release is installing were shown in English only. They are now translated into every device language.
- **Unreadable manifest** — a firmware manifest the hub could not read, or no check since Home Assistant started, reads as the reason nothing is offered instead of **Up to date**, and **Check for updates** shows an error from the release list.
- **Offline panel** — an offline panel, or a status the editor could not refresh, offers no **Install**; the device screen and the Updates sidebar say the values are the last ones read.
- **Failed install** — a failed firmware install clears once the panel reconnects with another firmware, and a second install while one runs is refused instead of reported as started.
- **Rollouts** — the dashboard notices a rollout another editor started, a finished rollout can be dismissed, and a rollout no longer waits on a device that was disabled or reloaded meanwhile.

### Integration

- **Device names** — the Home Assistant device that holds a panel's notify and update entities is named after the panel instead of "NSPanel HAUI Hub".
